newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Costa Rica report proposes sell-offs to ease debt.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rica report proposes sell-offs to ease debt.

text.p: A Costa Rica finance ministry special committee recommended on Thursday the sell-off of state assets to reduce the country's heavy internal debt burden.

The 80-page report, entitled "Problem and outlook for Costa Rica government debt. Tomorrow is too late", was elaborated over four months by former central bank governor Eduardo Lizano Fait, former finance minister Federico Vargas Peralta, economist Ronulfo Jimenez, banker Oscar Rodriguez and lawyer Marco Vinicio Tristan.
Its main recommendations were to sell off state-owned telephone, electricity generation, banking and alcohol production assets.
Costa Rica's internal debt is currently more than $2.5 billion, or about half the country's gross domestic product. It also has foreign debt of about $3.1 billion, according to the central bank.
President Jose Maria Figueres has called upon a panel of former Costa Rican presidents to advise him on how to handle the problem.
The 1987 Nobel Peace Laureate Oscar Arias, who was president from 1986 to 1990, said recently the internal debt could rise to $4 billion by the end of next year if action were not taken.
The former presidents, who met earlier this month, also recommended selling off state assets.

The finance ministry commission said the telecommunications system currently owned by the Costa Rican Electricity Institute (ICE), as well as ICE's power generation facilities, should be sold off along with the National Liquor Factory and three state-owned banks -- Banco de Costa Rica, Banco Credito Agricola de Cartago and Banco Internacional de Costa Rica.
The sell-off would be "the best path to proceed to reducing significantly the level of the government's internal debt," the report said. "Without this reduction the problem cannot be solved."
It said the sale process should begin immediately "given its technically complex and politically difficult" nature.
